comment: Memory offsets for Simutrans OTRP v50.1 - MUST be configured manually
IMPORTANT_NOTE: These offset values CANNOT be determined from source code alone.
They depend on compiler settings, optimization level, and binary structure.
You MUST find these values using ONE of these methods:
1. Use a debugger (gdb on Linux, x64dbg on Windows) - see docs/offset_configuration.md
2. Get values from Simutrans OTRP community for v50.1
3. Wait for automatic offset detection feature (coming soon)
Current status: ALL VALUES BELOW ARE PLACEHOLDERS (0x0000)
The tool WILL NOT WORK until you configure actual offsets!

karte_t.comment: World object - contains all game data
karte_t.convoi_array_description: Offset to vector_tpl<convoihandle_t> convoi_array in karte_t class
karte_t.halt_array_description: Offset to halt array in karte_t class (optional for basic functionality)
finding_instructions: In gdb: break karte_t::step, then print &((karte_t*)this)->convoi_array
Calculate offset: address of convoi_array - address of karte_t object

convoi_t.comment: Convoy object - represents a train/vehicle convoy
convoi_t.wait_lock_note: First member after virtual tables (24 bytes header on x64)
finding_instructions: print &((convoi_t*)this)->wait_lock  (should be ~+24 bytes from start on x64)
Calculate offsets from convoi_t object start address

vehicle_t.comment: Vehicle object - individual vehicle in a convoy
vehicle_t.note: Vehicle offsets are optional for basic train display functionality

haltestelle_t.name: 0x0000
haltestelle_t.note: Station offsets are optional for basic train display functionality

method_1_debugger.description: Use GDB (Linux) or x64dbg (Windows) to inspect memory
steps: 3. Set breakpoint in karte_t::step or convoi_t::step
4. When breakpoint hits, print addresses of members
6. Update this file with hexadecimal offsets
1. Check Simutrans OTRP forum or GitHub discussions
2. Search for 'v50.1 memory offsets' or 'v50.1 TiD configuration'
4. Replace this file with community-provided configuration

method_3_auto_discovery.note: Run: python offset_discovery.py --auto (coming in future version)

example_values_from_older_versions.note: These are EXAMPLE values only - DO NOT USE directly!

example_x64_offsets.convoi_t_wait_lock: Usually ~0x18 (24 bytes after start due to vtable)

example_values_from_older_versions.warning: Offsets change between versions! These examples are for reference only!

how_to_test: 5. If you see trains with correct names, offsets are correct!
6. If you see crashes or garbage data, offsets are wrong
